description: The U.S. Census Bureau and the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) publish three linked broadband products under federal broadband laws. The ACCESS BROADBAND Dashboard, created under the ACCESS BROADBAND Act of 2021, maps 21 indicators such as the share of households with a broadband subscription and of population where fixed service of at least 25/3 Mbps is available, next to employment, small business establishments, income, poverty, home values, migration, education and real GDP, for states, counties and, for some indicators, census tracts, including Puerto Rico; supplemental state, county and tract XLSX files carry estimates and margins of error. The Digital Equity Act Population Viewer and files give counts of the eight covered populations (for example low-income, aged 60 or over, rural or with a language barrier) used in NTIA's state funding formula, by state, county and tract. Local Estimates of Internet Adoption (LEIA) is an experimental model-based estimate of high-speed internet adoption for all 3,144 counties in 2022, from ACS microdata and FCC data. Access: web map viewers and XLSX or CSV downloads on www2.census.gov with quick guides; free and public domain. Caveats: sources are ACS 2017-2021 and FCC Form 477 data from 2019 for the dashboard, and only one dashboard release (2023) is posted although annual updates were planned; LEIA is experimental. Simulation uses: household broadband adoption as a dependency in telecom resilience and service-loss models, and equity weighting of digital infrastructure investment scenarios. Related records: ACS tables, FCC Form 477 deployment data and the Community Resilience Estimates.
